cards.back: Cutting each document into passages small enough to search precisely and cheap enough to put in a prompt, while keeping enough context that each still makes sense alone.

cards.front: Why chunking sets the ceiling on retrieval quality
cards.back: Every later step works on chunks: embeddings are per chunk, search returns chunks, citations point at chunks and the model reads chunks.
Splits by paragraphs, then sentences, then words, until each piece fits. A good general default, but blind to headings unless you add them.
One section per chunk, split further if too long. Best for wikis, policies and runbooks; merge very short sections.
Embeds sentences and cuts where the topic shifts. Useful for long unstructured text like transcripts, but ingestion is slower.
300 to 800 tokens with 10 to 20% overlap for fixed or recursive splitting, never bigger than the embedding model's input limit. Then measure.
A sentence that straddles a boundary stays whole in at least one chunk. It costs 10 to 20% more storage.
Prefix each chunk with the document title and heading path before embedding. Cheap, and the biggest single win on structured documents.
Index small child chunks for precise matching, and return their parent section to the model for context.
A stable chunk_id built from doc_id, version and position; the doc_id itself so deletes are one call; and the ACL so permissions are enforced in the query.
Keep small tables whole. Split big ones into row groups and repeat the header row in every group, or turn each row into a sentence.

quiz.q: Chunks for India and US "adoptive parents" rules look almost identical to search. What fixes it most cheaply?
choices: Prefix each chunk with its title and heading path
quiz.why: The heading path tells the embedding which country a chunk is about.

quiz.q: Why do very large chunks match many questions weakly?
choices: Their embedding becomes an average of several ideas
They exceed the vector database's row limit
Overlap makes them duplicate each other
quiz.why: A big chunk's vector drifts to the middle of its ideas, so it matches everything a little and nothing well.

quiz.q: When should you decide which metadata to attach?
choices: Only when a filter is needed
quiz.why: Adding a field later means re-parsing everything, so decide it up front.

quiz.q: Why build chunk_id from doc_id, version and position?
choices: It lets the model cite page numbers
Re-ingesting the same document overwrites instead of duplicating
quiz.why: A stable id means the same chunk lands on the same row every time it is ingested.

quiz.q: How should you choose chunk size and overlap?
choices: Use the setting with the fewest chunks
Sweep settings and compare recall@k on golden questions
Pick the largest size the model accepts
Copy the defaults of your framework and stop there
quiz.why: The page says don't guess: build 100 to 200 golden questions and sweep a few settings.

quiz.q: Two settings give recall@5 of 0.86 and 0.88, but the second uses far more prompt tokens. Which do you pick?
choices: The cheaper one, since it is within a point or two of the best
quiz.why: Prompt tokens are paid on every question, so pick the cheapest setting near the best recall.

choices: Split on functions and classes, with the file path in the header
quiz.why: Function and class boundaries are the natural seams in code.
